articles.title: Tuesday briefing: Europe thinks Russia is preparing to test Nato’s limits
articles.summary:
In today’s newsletter: Intelligence chiefs warn that Russia’s appetite for risk is growing, as sabotage and other covert attacks target countries supporting Ukraine

Good morning. As the UN general assembly kicks off in New York later today, we anticipate a heavy focus on the ongoing conflicts in Iran, Ukraine and the Gulf – as well as the inevitable body language analysis of Andy Burnham’s first in-person meeting with Donald Trump.

But another related conflict is likely to dominate informal discussions: the intensifying acts of sabotage on European states that are believed to trace back to Russia but deliberately fall below the threshold for military response – a so-called hybrid or “shadow war” with the singular purpose of disrupting support for Ukraine.

articles.title: UK to provide Saudi Arabia with military support against Houthis
articles.summary:
UK to provide Saudi Arabia with military support against Houthis

Submitted by MEE staff on Tue, 09/22/2026 - 10:15
Defence Minister Luke Pollard said support for the kingdom would comply with international humanitarian law
A security personnel stands guard during a ceremony organised by Houthi authorities to mark the 12th anniversary of takeover of Yemeni capital, in Sanaa on 20 September 2026 (Mohammed Huwais / AFP)
Off

The UK is set to provide military support to Saudi Arabia against the Houthi advance in Yemen and the group's strikes on the kingdom.

Defence Minister Luke Pollard said the UK would deploy the RAF Voyager plane - operating from a UK base in Cyprus - for "air-to-air refuelling" operations.

Saudi aircraft have been carrying out air strikes against Yemen's Houthis as the country's once-dormant war resumed earlier this month.

The move comes following a Saudi request for military support after the Houthis increased drone and missile attacks on the kingdom in recent weeks.

"We're doing it for national security reasons in support of our own national security," UK Defence Minister Luke Pollard told Sky News.

"In dangerous times, good friends stand together."

Pollard insisted the support would comply with international humanitarian law. A statement from the Ministry of Defence said the UK "has agreed to provide an RAF Voyager air-to-air refuelling aircraft to support Saudi defensive activity in support of the legitimate government of Yemen".

It added: "The Houthis are a dangerous threat to regional stability in the Middle East, and it is in the UK’s national economic and security interest that they do not succeed."

The air support follows the deployment of air defence equipment and UK military personnel to Saudi Arabia in recent weeks.

The Houthis have targeted Saudi cities, oil infrastructure and Red Sea oil shipments as they captured a swathe of the Red Sea coast in a lightning campaign, giving them control over the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait.

They are demanding an end to the decade-old Saudi blockade on Yemen, in return for which they say attacks on Saudi Arabia and its oil exports through the Red Sea will be halted.

The UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) announced on Tuesday that around 230,000 displaced persons in Yemen and another 10,000 refugees in Djibouti are expected to require humanitarian assistance in the coming months.

Pakistan says no plans for military action in Yemen after attacks on Saudi Arabia
Read More »

More than 130,000 people have been displaced in Yemen and some 3,000 have fled to Djibouti due to the resumption of fighting in early September between the Houthis and pro-government forces.

These figures could rise to 230,000 and 10,000 respectively in the coming months, UNHCR spokesperson Babar Baloch announced at a press briefing in Geneva.

Multiple sources told CNN on Sunday that despite the US providing additional intelligence and targeting support to Saudi Arabia, it is still unable to push back against Houthi forces.

Anonymous US officials who spoke to CNN said that for months, its intelligence reports indicated the Houthis would attempt to close another key waterway for commercial shipping as Iran did earlier this year.

But despite Saudi Arabia's reassurances for the last decade that it had given effective training to the Saudi-backed Yemeni government to fight the Houthis, according to two US officials, Washington still believes that Riyadh is not capable of pushing back the Houthis.

UK support for Saudi Arabia has been controversial, particularly after the country began launching air strikes on Yemen in 2015 in a war that killed more than 150,000 people.

articles.title: UN warns 230,000 Yemenis could be displaced if fighting continues
articles.summary:
UN warns 230,000 Yemenis could be displaced if fighting continues

More than 230,000 Yemenis could be displaced if fighting intensifies, the UNHCR representative for Yemen warned, raising fears about the humanitarian situation worsening. 

As many as 112,000 people have already been displaced due to the latest escalation, UN agencies said, with most of the displacement taking place in the last two weeks along Yemen’s western coast and in Taiz governorate. 

The warning comes amid fighting in western Yemen, with government forces saying the Saudi-led coalition carried out heavy air strikes on Houthi positions, gatherings and weapons stores west of Taiz province. 

The renewed fighting has also driven thousands of Yemenis across the Bab al-Mandeb Strait to Djibouti.

archive.security_status_cs: Konflikt v Rudém moři a Jemenu se vyhrotil po bleskové ofenzivě Houthiů, kteří ovládli západní pobřeží a strategickou úžinu Bab al-Mandab. Útoky na saúdská ropná zařízení a metropoli Riad podtrhují selhání regionálního odstrašení a hrozbu nových výpadků dodávek energií.
archive.security_status_en: The conflict in the Red Sea and Yemen has escalated sharply following a lightning Houthi offensive seizing Yemen's west coast and the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and Riyadh highlight failing regional deterrence and the ongoing threat of major energy supply disruptions.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další diplomatické manévry a hrozbu odvetných vojenských útoků USA a spojenců v reakci na houthiské útoky na Riad. Ceny ropy a tržní volatilita zůstanou na zvýšených úrovních kvůli obavám z širší regionální války.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further diplomatic maneuvers and the threat of retaliatory military strikes by the US and allies are expected in response to Houthi attacks on Riyadh. Oil prices and market volatility will remain elevated due to fears of a broader regional war.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v Rudém moři a okolí strategického průlivu Bab al-Mandab se prudce vyhrotila poté, co Houthiové zahájili bleskovou ofenzivu a útočí na saúdskou infrastrukturu včetně metropole Riad. Británie poskytuje Saúdské Arábii vojenskou podporu formou doplňování paliva za letu, zatímco G7 tlačí na Irán, aby zastavil vyzbrojování povstalců.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Red Sea and around the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait has escalated sharply as the Houthis launched a lightning offensive and targeted Saudi infrastructure, including Riyadh. Britain is providing military air-to-air refueling support to Saudi Arabia, while the G7 pressures Iran to halt its arming of the rebels.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další vojenské eskalace a diplomatické přetahované před Valným shromážděním OSN, přičemž ceny ropy a tržní volatilita zůstanou vysoké.
archive.forecast_en: Further military escalations and diplomatic tussles ahead of the UN General Assembly are expected over the coming days, keeping oil prices and market volatility high.
